name: Diyaluma Falls
description: The second-highest waterfall in Sri Lanka, famous for its multiple upper natural pools where visitors can swim right on the edge of the roaring drop.

name: Bambarakanda Falls
description: Standing at a majestic 263 meters, this is the tallest waterfall in Sri Lanka, cascading down a sheer vertical cliff surrounded by serene pine forests.

name: Ravana Falls
description: A highly popular and easily accessible multi-tier waterfall in Ella, linked to the epic Ramayana legend and offering dramatic flow during the rainy season.

name: Dunhinda Falls
description: Known as the 'Bridal Fall' for its smoky water spray, this 63-meter cascade is reached via a scenic jungle trek near Badulla town.

name: Devon Falls
description: Nicknamed the 'Veil of the Valley', this 97-meter multi-tiered waterfall cascades gracefully opposite lush tea plantations along the Hatton-Nuwara Eliya road.

name: St. Clair's Falls
description: Widely known as the 'Little Niagara of Sri Lanka', this is one of the widest waterfalls in the country, formed by the Kotmale Oya river.

name: Baker's Falls
description: Located inside Horton Plains National Park, this 20-meter cascade is surrounded by misty cloud forest vegetation and wild rhododendrons.

name: Laxapana Falls
description: Standing 126 meters tall, this powerful waterfall in Maskeliya is steeped in local folklore and crucial to Sri Lanka's hydroelectric power generation.

name: Aberdeen Falls
description: A striking 98-meter waterfall nestled deep in Ginigathena, featuring a massive rock face and a deep natural plunge pool at its base.

name: Ramboda Falls
description: A high-altitude 109-meter waterfall split into upper and lower sections, easily viewed from the A5 highway near Pussellawa.

name: Lover's Leap Waterfall
description: A romantic 30-meter waterfall originating from Sri Lanka's highest peak (Pidurutalagala), accessible via tea estate paths near Nuwara Eliya town.

name: Bomburu Ella
description: Also known as Perawella Falls, this is a vast network of multi-branching jungle cascades considered one of the widest waterfall clusters in the country.

name: Bopath Ella
description: Named for its unique physical resemblance to a sacred Bo leaf, this 30-meter cascade in Kuruwita is a popular weekend picnic spot.

name: Kirindi Ella
description: Tucked away in Pelmadulla, this 116-meter tall cascade tumbles into a deep pool surrounded by dense forest foliage.

name: Surathali Ella
description: A 60-meter high fall named after a famous old Sinhala movie filmed on-location, conveniently located right beside the Colombo-Batticaloa highway.

name: Olu Ella
description: The 6th highest waterfall in Sri Lanka (127m), dropping in multiple gentle, white steps that resemble a blooming water lily (Olu).

name: Asupini Ella
description: A dramatic 30-meter high waterfall near Aranayaka, linked to ancient legends of royal consorts and surrounding mountain vistas.

name: Sera Ella
description: Hidden within the Knuckles Mountain Range, famous for a natural rock cave hidden directly behind the cascading curtain of water.

name: Hunas Falls
description: A picturesque 60-meter high waterfall located near Elkaduwa, originating from the Matale forest hills above a luxury resort area.

name: Huluganga Falls
description: Located directly by the main road in Huluganga town, this 75-meter cascade plunges off massive boulders fed by streams from the Knuckles range.
